title: Maybank Falls Below RM10 for First Time in Nine Months as Rising Bond Yields Hurt Banking Stocks
body: KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 1): Malayan Banking Bhd (KL:MAYBANK) fell below RM10 for the first time in nearly nine months and banking stocks mostly declined on Thursday amid rising bond yields. Higher yields generally hurt banks as they take larger paper losses from lower prices of the bonds they hold, which eats into capital and forces them to book losses if they sell. Investors may also demand higher returns on corporate bonds, affecting appetite for new issuances. That would weigh on banks’ near term non-interest income as well as their capital ratios, Affin Hwang Investment Bank flagged in a note on Thursday. Maybank, the country’s top bank in terms of assets, fell for the third straight day and closed down 0.4% at RM9.95. CIMB Group Holdings Bhd (KL:CIMB) and Hong Leong Bank Bhd (KL:HLBANK) each declined over 1%. title: UOB Malaysia, RHB Banking and Maybank execute landmark MYOR-based transaction
body: PETALING JAYA: UOB Malaysia, RHB Banking Group and Malayan Banking (Maybank) recently executed the first Malaysia Overnight Rate-based three-month interbank money market transaction in the country, incorporating a two-day lookback calculation convention through an interbank money market broker. The landmark transaction was anchored by UOB Malaysia and executed with RHB and Maybank, marking a significant milestone in the evolution of Malaysia’s money market and supporting industry efforts towards the adoption of risk-free rate-based market conventions. The transaction enhances transparency and price discovery by making funding levels and spreads visible to a broader network of market participants. This contrasts with bilateral transactions, where pricing information is limited to the counterparties involved. By helping establish a transparent Malaysia Overnight Rate (MYOR) funding curve and an observable reference point for three-month interbank funding, the transaction improves visibility into funding spreads over MYOR and banks’ cost of borrowing, supporting more efficient pricing across the wider market. UOB Malayia corporate and investment banking country head Christina Cheah said, “The successful execution of this money market transaction reflects the strong collaboration between UOB Malaysia, RHB and Maybank in supporting the evolution of the country’s financial markets. By establishing a transparent benchmark for MYOR-based funding, we are contributing to greater price discovery and helping to build confidence in the adoption of risk-free rate conventions. “As a leading foreign bank in the country, UOB Malaysia remains committed to partnering local market participants, sharing regional expertise and supporting initiatives that strengthen market resilience and align the domestic financial ecosystem with global standards.” The transaction references MYOR compounded in arrears with a two-day lookback mechanism, providing operational certainty in interest calculations while remaining anchored to actual market transactions. RHB Banking Group wholesale banking managing director Nurjesmi Mohd Nashir said, “This transaction demonstrates how market participants can work together to put MYOR-based conventions into practice and support the continued development of Malaysia’s money market. “As the industry progresses towards the transition from KLIBOR to MYOR, it is important that we build practical market experience and develop conventions that can be adopted more widely. RHB is committed to supporting Bank Negara Malaysia’s efforts to develop a deeper and more efficient MYOR market, and to playing an active role in the continued development of Malaysia’s financial markets.” Farid Kairi, deputy group CEO of global banking and managing director of global markets said: “Maybank is pleased to have played an integral role in this inaugural MYOR-based money market transaction. It marks an important first step in establishing the foundation for deeper liquidity, while setting the stage for widening the aperture for more MYOR-linked solutions and supporting robust price discovery for market participants. “This achievement reflects the collective efforts of industry participants and Bank Negara Malaysia in strengthening Malaysia’s financial market infrastructure.” Bank Negara Malaysia introduced MYOR in September 2021 as Malaysia’s Alternative Reference Rate (ARR). MYOR is calculated as the volume-weighted average rate of actual unsecured overnight ringgit interbank transactions, providing a robust benchmark grounded in deep and liquid overnight funding markets. The transition towards MYOR aligns Malaysia with other major financial markets that have adopted overnight risk-free rates including Singapore, Japan, Switzerland, the United States and the United Kingdom.

title: MGS sell-off set to hit RHB's Q3 earnings: HLIB
body: KUALA LUMPUR: RHB Bank Bhd's near-term earnings are likely to come under pressure from higher Malaysian Government Securities (MGS) yields, said Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB) Research. Analyst Raymond Ng said the recent spike in MGS yields would likely hurt trading income in the third quarter of financial year 2026 (Q3 FY26), with limited time left in the quarter for a recovery. He said stronger contributions from wealth management, bancassurance/takaful, investment banking, broking and loan-related fees should provide some cushion but are unlikely to fully offset the trading income weakness. "The impact should be viewed more as foregone trading upside rather than outsized losses, given RHB's relatively small trading book," he said in a note. Ng said RHB's treasury division had also been tactically unwinding securities positions, crystallising gains where possible while reducing exposure. However, the bank's management remained more positive on the fourth quarter, with scope to reposition the portfolio and capture opportunities if bond yields stabilise or retreat. Despite the near-term earnings pressure, management maintained its return on equity (ROE) target of 10.8 per cent to 11 per cent, supported by about six per cent loan growth, cost growth of no more than one per cent and benign credit costs. Ng said the target remained within reach, although RHB was more likely to end up at the lower end of the range. Credit costs are tracking at around 13 basis points, at the lower end of management's 13 to 14 basis points guidance, while wealth sales rose 35 per cent year-on-year as of June 2026. On asset quality, Ng said there were no major red flags, with deterioration in the small and medium enterprise (SME) segment remaining gradual and manageable. "Gross impaired loan formation continues to stem largely from SME and community banking, although management has not seen a meaningful acceleration in stress," he said. He added that RHB remained selective in mortgage and SME lending and was not chasing growth through aggressive pricing where risk-adjusted returns were unattractive. Meanwhile, capital management remains a medium-term catalyst, with management targeting greater clarity on its capital and dividend policy by the first quarter of 2027. Ng said a potential 100-basis-point uplift in RHB's common equity tier-one ratio following the Basel III reforms in January 2028 could translate into about RM2 billion of additional capital. However, any excess capital return would depend on the group's growth requirements and ability to maintain its CET1 ratio at around current levels. HLIB maintained its "Hold" call on RHB with an unchanged target price of RM8, based on an implied 1.0 times the calendar year 2027 price-to-book ratio. RHB currently offers a projected FY27 dividend yield of more than 6.5 per cent, while a potential increase in the overnight policy rate from 2.75 per cent to three per cent in 2027 could provide another earnings boost.

title: Expedite political will to guarantee people’s right to know
body: On the International Day for Universal Access to Information on 28 September, the Centre for Independent Journalism (CIJ), Article 19 and the Center to Combat Corruption and Cronyism (C4 Center) call on the Malaysian government and Parliament to make the right to access information a meaningful and accessible right, and not merely a promise of reform. The UN has designated this year’s theme as ‘Upholding information integrity in the digital age: the role of access to information in addressing information disorder’. Reliable, timely and credible public information is essential to informed participation, accountability and trust in public institutions. Malaysia stands at a critical juncture. Parliament is considering the nation’s first federal freedom of information law, while serious questions remain about the transparency, legal basis, and implementation of Najib Razak’s conditional pardon and house arrest. These are not separate transparency failures. They expose the same problem: Malaysians cannot hold institutions accountable when the government makes decisions behind a wall of secrecy. We acknowledge the government’s decision to introduce a federal Freedom of Information Bill and welcome its referral to a parliamentary special select committee following its first reading in July 2026. However, as our organisations have stated, the bill, as tabled, falls far short of what ordinary people should expect from landmark transparency legislation. The Centre for Law and Democracy’s assessment subsequently gave the bill 47 out of 150 points under its right to information rating methodology, highlighting the extent to which the proposed framework needs improvement. - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member The bill must be strengthened into an enforceable right to know act, consistent with Article 10(1)(a) of the Federal Constitution, international law and standards and the recommendations of Malaysian and international civil society. Malaysia must end the culture of secrecy that continues to shield the exercise of power from public scrutiny. The government cannot credibly champion transparency while limiting the public’s access to information about decisions of profound public interest, including from the laws governing access to information itself. The government must demonstrate its political will and commitment to transparency by applying these principles across the board and not letting them remain mere lip service to garner votes. On this International Day for Universal Access to Information, we call on the government and Parliament to act. The government and Parliament must: Strengthen the bill, currently under the purview of the special select committee, into an enforceable right to know act, consistent with international laws and standards and the recommendations from civil society groups. It must: - Uphold the constitutional guarantee under Article 10(1)(a) of the Federal Constitution and guarantee freedom of information as a pre-condition to the realisation of the freedom of expression and speech - Make disclosure the rule and secrecy the exception, with narrowly defined exemptions based on demonstrable harm and subject to a strong public-interest override - Ensure the freedom of information law cannot be undermined by existing secrecy provisions, including the Official Secrets Act - Remove unnecessary restrictions on who can request information and ensure everyone can exercise the right without having to demonstrate a particular interest or purpose - Establish a freedom of information commission as an independent oversight body, with the power to review refusals, order disclosure and monitor the implementation of the freedom of information law - Require proactive disclosure of information and documents of significant public interest - Make the parliamentary freedom of information process transparent and participatory, including publication of submissions, recommendations and the revised bill Guarantee prompt disclosure and publication of the documents necessary for the public to understand the decision regarding the conditional pardon of Najib Razak, as demanded by CIJ and other civil society organisations, including: - The relevant pardons board minutes - The Attorney General’s written submission, subject only to narrowly justified redactions - The full conditions governing the house arrest arrangement - The legal basis for implementing house arrest and its relationship with existing laws - The mechanisms for monitoring and enforcing compliance - Significant public expenditure associated with the arrangement. These demands do not challenge the constitutional existence of the power of pardon. They demand transparency about the exercise and implementation of authority’s power. Constitutional powers are not a licence for institutional secrecy. The Government has repeatedly committed itself to institutional reform, good governance and restoring public confidence. The test of those commitments is whether transparency is upheld when disclosure is difficult, politically sensitive or institutionally consequential. We believe that a freedom of information law that leaves the underlying culture of secrecy intact will not deliver meaningful reform. In the spirit of this international day, we call on Malaysia to move from promises of transparency to a legally enforceable culture of openness. Ordinary people have the right to know. Disclosure of information held by government and public authorities is necessary to scrutinise the exercise of public power. This ensures that no institution is beyond legitimate public accountability. The right to information is not a concession from government. It is a foundation of accountable government. This legislation is essential to guarantee the public’s collective right to be informed by public authorities about important aspects of their functioning; the right to seek or request information; and the right to be informed and to receive information about various aspects of the public sphere. We are also pleased to launch our campaign demonstrating the level of support from our MPs for the guarantee of a robust bill. Look out for more information on our social media in the coming days. Issued by: - Wathshlah Naidu, Centre for Independent Journalism - Nalini Elumalai, Article 19 - Prishanth Linggaraj, C4 Center The views expressed in Aliran's media statements and the NGO statements we have endorsed reflect Aliran's official stand. Views and opinions expressed in other pieces published here do not necessarily reflect Aliran's official position.

In the spirit of this international day, we call on Malaysia to move from promises of transparency to a legally enforceable culture of openness. Ordinary people have the right to know. Disclosure of information held by government and public authorities is necessary to scrutinise the exercise of public power. This ensures that no institution is beyond legitimate public accountability. The right to information is not a concession from government. It is a foundation of accountable government. This legislation is essential to guarantee the public’s collective right to be informed by public authorities about important aspects of their functioning; the right to seek or request information; and the right to be informed and to receive information about various aspects of the public sphere. We are also pleased to launch our campaign demonstrating the level of support from our MPs for the guarantee of a robust bill. Look out for more information on our social media in the coming days. title: DNB secures RM5.2 bil for next phase of 5G growth, MOF retains special share
body: Digital Nasional Berhad (DNB) has completed a RM5.2 billion financing exercise as it moves into the next phase of Malaysia’s 5G development. The financing comes as the nation’s first 5G network has secured a new long-term spectrum assignment, while the government (via MOF Inc) will exit as an ordinary shareholder. CelcomDigi, Maxis and YTL are expected to hold equal ownership in DNB. Transition is expected to be completed in early Q4 2026, however, MOF Inc. will retain a special share. DNB completes RM5.2 billion financing DNB said it has completed a RM5.2 billion Syndicated Islamic Term Financing exercise, which it described as among the largest syndicated loan facilities ever arranged for an unlisted company in Malaysia. Maybank Investment Bank acted as Mandated Lead Arranger, Bookrunner and Coordinating Arranger, while AmInvestment Bank, CIMB Islamic Bank, RHB Islamic Bank and United Overseas Bank Malaysia were Joint Mandated Lead Arrangers. AmInvestment Bank also acted as financial adviser to DNB. The financing will also be used to refinance DNB’s Government Guarantee Revolving Credit Facility (GGRCF), which expired on 29 September 2026. According to DNB, the new financing provides a sustainable long-term funding structure to support its future growth. The financing is also expected to reduce the need for additional equity funding from DNB’s mobile network operator shareholders, based on DNB’s current regulatory commitments and funding requirements. DNB CEO Datuk Azman Ismail said, “The successful completion of this RM5.2 billion financing exercise marks a significant milestone for DNB and reflects strong confidence in our business fundamentals, operational track record and long-term role in Malaysia’s digital economy. This financing provides DNB with a sustainable platform to operate on its own, continue investing in network enhancement and capacity expansion, and leverage our expanded spectrum assets.” He added, “As Malaysia progresses under the dual network framework, DNB remains committed to providing world-class digital infrastructure that supports our shareholders, customers, enterprises and government agencies. With strong financing, enhanced spectrum resources and a proven nationwide 5G platform, DNB is well positioned to support the Government’s AI Nation aspirations and help power Malaysia’s next phase of digital growth.” DNB gets 15-year 5G spectrum certainty DNB has also received the full 100MHz block in the 3.3GHz to 3.4GHz band, known as F0, while its entire 240MHz spectrum holding has been converted from Apparatus Assignment (AA) into Spectrum Assignment (SA). The Spectrum Assignment for a 15-year period awarded by the MCMC provides greater long-term certainty over spectrum availability and it takes effect from 1 October 2026. By securing 200MHz of the contiguous mid-band spectrum (3.3 to 3.5GHz), DNB has a stronger foundation to modernise the network, expand indoor building solutions, enhance coverage and maximise spectrum utilisation. In addition, DNB also has 2x 20Hz blocks of the low band spectrum with 703MHz to 723MHz and 758Hz to 778MHz. DNB said its spectrum holdings will also support higher network capacity and efficiency, as well as technologies including Massive MIMO, carrier aggregation, 5G Advanced and AI-driven network capabilities. MOF to retain special share in DNB While the recent financing facilitates MOF Inc.’s planned exit as an ordinary shareholder of DNB, the government via MOF Inc will continue to retain a special share in the company. According to DNB, the special share will safeguard national interests and ensure continued stewardship over key strategic matters. Following the share transfer, the mobile network operator shareholders would assume a greater role in jointly steering DNB’s strategic and operational priorities. In a separate statement issued by CelcomDigi, the telco says it will bring its scale, nationwide network assets and more than 30 years of telecommunications experience to support DNB. This includes leveraging on existing infrastructure, sites and capabilities to drive cost efficiencies, support coverage expansion and accelerate indoor 5G deployment.

body: SHAH ALAM (Sept 30): Genneva Gold Sdn Bhd, the company behind a massive gold investment scam, has been wound up by the High Court here, which could see victims recouping their losses.  In her brief judgment on Wednesday, Justice Wan Fadhilah Nor Wan Idris found that the company, which had been convicted for unlawful deposit-taking, had lost its foundation as it had ceased operations for many years and lacked the licences and permits to resume its original business.  The court also noted the deficiencies in its records and that the company did not have a functioning board of directors.  The court granted the winding-up order and confirmed interim liquidator Wong Weng Foo to his role in dissolving the firm.  Ng Wan Yee, who holds a major stake of 750,000 shares in the company, had moved to wind up the company in August 2024, to prevent other company directors from removing more than RM21 million in released company assets.  The move follows a Sessions Court order on June 28, 2024, that revoked seizure orders under anti-money laundering laws on millions of ringgit and approximately 28.3kg of gold bars.  In her petition, Wan Yee said there was a "high likelihood" that functional directors or other relevant parties might dissipate these assets for personal benefit rather than settling claims of thousands of investors.  She claimed that some directors had already attempted to "siphon monies" under the guise of paying professional fees.  An opposing creditor, Liew Chio Chuan, a 25% shareholder of Genneva, had challenged the appointment of Wong, arguing there was "material non-disclosure" by Wan Yee and that there was "no real danger" of assets being lost before a formal hearing before the court.  Central to the dispute was the movement of funds just days before the petition was filed.  Records show that following the release of the seizure orders, Genneva's directors had authorised the transfer of RM11,659,661.20 from accounts at Maybank and Public Bank to a stakeholder account held by the company’s long-time solicitors, Messrs Gooi & Azura.  The solicitors and Maybank have justified the transfers, citing a board resolution dated June 26, 2024, and "letters of authorisation" dating back to 2016. They maintain the bank was unaware of the pending winding-up petition at the time.  Genneva Gold and its top executives were found guilty in August 2020 of illegally taking tens of million in deposits. The company was fined RM450 million and various executives were also jailed and slapped with fines amounting to hundreds of millions of ringgit.  Former Prime Minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad launched Genneva Malaysia Sdn Bhd’s "syariah-compliant" gold trading scheme on Dec 15, 2010.

body: Nor Rashidi (tengah), Profesor Dr. Shamsul Bahari (dua kanan), Imbran (kiri) dan Nur Iman (kanan) bergambar kenangan bersama pelajar yang menjayakan Program Maybank Global CR Day 2026: “Cahaya Future Ready” LABUAN: Maybank International Labuan Branch dengan kerjasama Bahagian Hal Ehwal Pelajar UMSKAL telah menganjurkan Program Maybank Global CR Day 2026 yang diadakan di Dewan Theatrette, Universiti Malaysia Sabah Kampus Antarabangsa Labuan (UMSKAL) pada Sabtu. Program yang berlangsung sehari itu bertujuan memberi pendedahan serta motivasi kepada pelajar sekolah menengah mengenai peluang melanjutkan pelajaran ke peringkat lebih tinggi. Majlis berkenaan turut diserikan dengan kehadiran Pengurus Besar Cawangan Maybank International Labuan, Nor Rashidi Mohammad, Pengarah UMSKAL, Prof. Dr. Shamsul Bahari Shamsudin dan Timbalan Pengarah Sektor Pembangunan Murid, Jabatan Pendidikan Wilayah Persekutuan Labuan, Imbran Yunus serta Ketua Bahagian Hal Ehwal Pelajar UMSKAL, Nur Iman Reedzal. Program itu dijayakan 40 pelajar Tingkatan 5 dari lapan buah sekolah menengah di Wilayah Persekutuan Labuan. Antara pengisian utama ialah sesi interaktif berkaitan saluran dan cara memohon ke institusi pengajian tinggi, termasuk Foundation/Diploma UMS, Matrikulasi, Form 6, Institut Perguruan Guru (IPG) dan Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET). Selain sesi motivasi dan perkongsian pengalaman, peserta turut dibawa melawat sekitar kampus UMSKAL bagi memberi gambaran sebenar kehidupan universiti. Dalam semangat tanggungjawab sosial korporat, pihak Maybank turut menyumbangkan dana kepada Dapur Siswa UMSKAL yang disampaikan Nor Rashidi kepada Prof. Dr. Shamsul Bahari sebagai inisiatif membantu pelajar B40 di kampus. Program ini menjadi platform strategik memperkukuh hubungan antara sektor korporat dan pendidikan tinggi, sekaligus menyemai semangat kesukarelawan serta kesiapsiagaan pelajar menghadapi masa depan yang lebih cerah.

title: AG Cautions on Use of AI, Effective Human Oversight Is Still Essential
body: KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): While the emergence of artificial intelligence (AI) has been used extensively and relied upon in the last few years, Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar cautioned for the need for human oversight in its usage. Dusuki said there is no doubt that AI offers significant opportunities in various sectors. For instance, he said, in healthcare, it can assist clinical judgement while in the corporate sphere, it can support decision-making, improve efficiency, and help professionals process increasingly complex information. “But as our reliance on these systems grows, so, too, does the importance of understanding how they are used and how they are governed. We need to ask some very practical questions: How reliable is the information produced by an AI system? What are the limits of its capabilities? Who is responsible for checking its output?” he said. He questioned what would happen when the AI system does not perform as expected. “These are not merely questions about technology. They are questions of governance, professional responsibility, and human oversight. Increasingly, they may also have consequences for legal liability and insurance. “For any institution adopting AI, it is therefore important to understand why the technology is being used, what risks may arise from its use, and what safeguards are necessary. Technology may assist professional judgement, but effective human oversight remains essential,” he reminded. Dusuki was delivering his keynote address at the Inaugural Financial Lines Forum at a hotel here. Also present were Lembaga Tabung Haji chairman and RHB Bank founder Tan Sri Abdul Rashid Hussin, who delivered a special address, and former Federal Court judge Tan Sri Zainun Ali, former Chief Judge of Malaya Tan Sri Hasnah Mohamed Hashim, as well as former and current judges. The AG said that while there are continuing issues in the usage of AI, there is a need to use it responsibly. Dusuki said the use of AI requires engagement among those who develop the technology, those who deploy it, those who rely on it, and those who assess and manage the risks associated with its use. Hence, he welcomed the organisation of such a forum like the Financial Lines forum as it brings together legal professionals, healthcare practitioners, corporate leaders, insurers, brokers, and other stakeholders. “We have an opportunity to learn from one another, to better understand the risks and opportunities before us, and to consider how our respective professions can respond responsibly to a rapidly changing environment. “Ultimately, the question is not simply what artificial intelligence can do. The more important question is, how we, as professionals, choose to use it responsibly,” he added. The one-day forum gathers medical experts, insurers, lawyers, and judges in exchanging views on medical negligence, governance, and AI. Meanwhile, in her welcoming address, Zainun, the chairperson for the Financial Lines forum, said a decision made in a boardroom may engage directors' duties, regulatory standards, disclosure obligations, and insurance coverage. “The adoption of AI in a hospital may raise questions of clinical judgement, patient safety, informed consent, data governance, institutional responsibility, and professional indemnity. “A claim may begin as a private dispute, but reveal a broader weakness in governance, documentation, communication, and risk management. No single profession has all the answers. Judges see how disputes crystallise and how legal principles operate in real cases. Regulators see patterns across institutions and markets. Lawyers advise on duties, responsibility, and remedy,” she said. Zainun added that directors and general counsel confront the practical demands of governance. “Doctors and hospital leaders carry responsibility for patient care. Insurers and reinsurers and brokers understand how emerging risks are assessed, transferred, and ultimately borne. “Sound risk management begins before a claim arises by identifying exposures, strengthening safeguards, and preparing for the consequences of loss. title: Asteel names ex-IGP Razarudin chairman, Clifford Hii executive deputy chairman in board revamp
body: Asteel names ex-IGP Razarudin chairman, Clifford Hii executive deputy chairman in board revamp KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): Asteel Group Bhd (KL:ASTEEL) has appointed former Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Razarudin Husain @ Abd Rasid as independent non-executive chairman and new controlling shareholder Datuk Clifford Hii Toh Leong as executive deputy chairman. The boardroom reshuffle follows Clifford securing a 53.08% stake in Asteel at the closing of a mandatory offer on Monday via investment vehicle Hii Capital Holdings Sdn Bhd. Clifford emerged as Asteel’s controlling shareholder in August with the acquisition of an initial 52.94% stake in the company via a RM20.75 million cash deal at 7.5 sen apiece. This triggered a mandatory offer for the remaining 47.06% stake in Asteel, also at 7.5 sen apiece. Clifford, 43, the son of the journalist-turned-businessman Tan Sri Clement Hii Chii Kok, who is the founder and executive chairman of property developer HCK Capital Group Bhd (KL:HCK) and group managing director and major shareholder of private education group SEG International. Clement is also the founder of Gambit Group Sdn Bhd, whose subsidiaries are involved in information technology services, investment, business management consultancy and is a registered digital asset custodian under the Securities Commission Malaysia. Clifford, a former non-independent, non-executive director at HCK Capital, has more than 20 years of experience in the education, property and financial technology sectors. He had held senior management and board positions covering corporate strategy, business development, corporate deals and investments, corporate governance and project management. Razarudin, 63, who is also independent non-executive chairman of Advancecon Holdings Bhd (KL:ADVCON), brings more than four decades of experience in national security and law enforcement. He was Malaysia’s 14th police chief until his retirement in June 2025. In separate filings, the steel manufacturer announced the appointment of Esther Teh Oun Pheng and Datuk Dr Lor Chee Leng as independent non-executive directors, while former executive chairman Tan Sri (Dr) Soh Thian Lai has been redesignated as executive director cum chairman emeritus. At the same time, non-independent non-executive director Christopher Hii Lu Ming, and independent non-executive directors Yan Ying Chieh, Khor Hun Nee and Wee Hiang Chyn have resigned, all citing personal reasons. Teh, 47, is head of internal audit and risk management at Usaha Tegas Sdn Bhd and an independent director of Nasdaq-listed OMS Energy Technologies Inc. She has more than 20 years of experience in internal and external audit, risk management, management consulting, shared-services implementation and operations and controllership. Her previous roles include group head of internal audit and compliance at Singapore-listed fintech company Silverlake Axis Ltd, head of risk management and assurance for group digital at Petroliam Nasional Bhd, and senior manager of management consulting at Accenture. Lor, 62, meanwhile, currently serves as an adviser to the Global ESG Leadership Organization and to Cambodia’s Ministry of Economy and Finance. He brings more than 35 years of experience in financial services, including banking transformation and strategy, corporate governance, risk management, credit oversight and consumer banking. His previous positions include independent director of Mizuho Bank (Malaysia) Bhd, chief executive officer and executive director of Canadia Bank PLC in Cambodia, group CEO of EON Bank Bhd, director of banking solutions at Hewlett Packard Enterprise, group head of consumer banking at RHB Bank Bhd and managing director of consumer banking at DBS Bank Ltd. At Tuesday's market close, Asteel shares rose a sen or 10.5% to 10.5 sen, valuing the group at RM50.9 million. The content is a snapshot from Publisher. title: Equal work, equal pay
body: I guess Lim Guan Eng, the former finance minister and now adviser to the Democratic Action Party (DAP), has a soft spot for employers. His call to exclude migrant workers from the minimum wage and the paltry 2% contribution to the Employees Provident Fund (EPF) repeats a position he took in early August 2025. Even then, labour groups criticised it. Since he has chosen to lend his voice to employers, be they micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) or others, it is apt to remind him of three fundamental issues. All people are equal Article 8(1) of the Federal Constitution treats everyone as equal and entitles them to equal protection. The courts have noted this. In Ahmad Zahri bin Mirza Abdul Hamid v AIMS Cyberjaya Sdn Bhd, the Federal Court took cognisance of Article 10 of the International Labour Organization (ILO) Migrant Workers (Supplementary Provisions) Convention 143 of 1975. It said Malaysia should promote and guarantee equality of opportunity and treatment between migrant workers and nationals. Referring to the convention, the court said: - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member Based on the above reasons we take the view that all workers should be treated with fairness, dignity and equality without distinction whether they are locals or foreigners. This is also consonant with Article 8(1) of the Federal Constitution which essentially provides that all persons are equal before the law and entitled to the equal protection of the law. his judgment alone should put to rest the flawed argument that Malaysia should adopt discriminatory standards against migrant workers to protect employers. Legislative protection Section 69F of the Employment Act 1955 empowers the director general of labour to inquire into and decide any dispute over discrimination in employment. An employer who fails to comply with the director general’s order faces, on conviction, a fine of up to RM50,000. For a continuing offence, there is a further fine of up to RM1,000 for each day it continues. Where an employer has signed a collective agreement with a trade union, section 17(1)(b) of the Industrial Relations Act 1967 makes it binding once the Industrial Court takes cognisance of it. It covers all worker employed in the undertaking, now or later. Industrial Court and other judicial decisions have affirmed that such agreements apply to migrant workers. International standards From the Universal Declaration of Human Rights to the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights (ICESCR) and the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, one fact stands unchallenged – there is no room for discriminatory employment practices against migrant workers. Full stop! No reasonable person would dispute that people doing the same work must receive the same pay. The right to equal pay for equal work should never be compromised. Doing so would destroy the foundation of equality, good conscience and fair treatment of workers, whether migrant or local. Working people need greater protection against the ever-rising cost of living, low and stagnant wages and inadequate retirement savings in the EPF. They do not need more protection for employers. Seeking such protection for employers is like asking workers to wallow in a vicious low-wage ecosystem so that employers can profit from staying in business. To even entertain the thought that businesses should be protected by treating migrant workers as second-class employees is heartless, an affront to human dignity and devoid of any sense of justice. title: DNB secures RM5.2 bil for next phase of 5G growth, MOF retains special share
body: Digital Nasional Berhad (DNB) has completed a RM5.2 billion financing exercise as it moves into the next phase of Malaysia’s 5G development. The financing comes as the nation’s first 5G network has secured a new long-term spectrum assignment, while the government (via MOF Inc) will exit as an ordinary shareholder. CelcomDigi, Maxis and YTL are expected to hold equal ownership in DNB. Transition is expected to be completed in early Q4 2026, however, MOF Inc. will retain a special share. DNB completes RM5.2 billion financing DNB said it has completed a RM5.2 billion Syndicated Islamic Term Financing exercise, which it described as among the largest syndicated loan facilities ever arranged for an unlisted company in Malaysia. Maybank Investment Bank acted as Mandated Lead Arranger, Bookrunner and Coordinating Arranger, while AmInvestment Bank, CIMB Islamic Bank, RHB Islamic Bank and United Overseas Bank Malaysia were Joint Mandated Lead Arrangers. AmInvestment Bank also acted as financial adviser to DNB. The financing will also be used to refinance DNB’s Government Guarantee Revolving Credit Facility (GGRCF), which expired on 29 September 2026. According to DNB, the new financing provides a sustainable long-term funding structure to support its future growth. The financing is also expected to reduce the need for additional equity funding from DNB’s mobile network operator shareholders, based on DNB’s current regulatory commitments and funding requirements. DNB CEO Datuk Azman Ismail said, “The successful completion of this RM5.2 billion financing exercise marks a significant milestone for DNB and reflects strong confidence in our business fundamentals, operational track record and long-term role in Malaysia’s digital economy. This financing provides DNB with a sustainable platform to operate on its own, continue investing in network enhancement and capacity expansion, and leverage our expanded spectrum assets.” He added, “As Malaysia progresses under the dual network framework, DNB remains committed to providing world-class digital infrastructure that supports our shareholders, customers, enterprises and government agencies. With strong financing, enhanced spectrum resources and a proven nationwide 5G platform, DNB is well positioned to support the Government’s AI Nation aspirations and help power Malaysia’s next phase of digital growth.” DNB gets 15-year 5G spectrum certainty DNB has also received the full 100MHz block in the 3.3GHz to 3.4GHz band, known as F0, while its entire 240MHz spectrum holding has been converted from Apparatus Assignment (AA) into Spectrum Assignment (SA). The Spectrum Assignment for a 15-year period awarded by the MCMC provides greater long-term certainty over spectrum availability and it takes effect from 1 October 2026. By securing 200MHz of the contiguous mid-band spectrum (3.3 to 3.5GHz), DNB has a stronger foundation to modernise the network, expand indoor building solutions, enhance coverage and maximise spectrum utilisation. In addition, DNB also has 2x 20Hz blocks of the low band spectrum with 703MHz to 723MHz and 758Hz to 778MHz. DNB said its spectrum holdings will also support higher network capacity and efficiency, as well as technologies including Massive MIMO, carrier aggregation, 5G Advanced and AI-driven network capabilities. MOF to retain special share in DNB While the recent financing facilitates MOF Inc.’s planned exit as an ordinary shareholder of DNB, the government via MOF Inc will continue to retain a special share in the company. According to DNB, the special share will safeguard national interests and ensure continued stewardship over key strategic matters. Following the share transfer, the mobile network operator shareholders would assume a greater role in jointly steering DNB’s strategic and operational priorities. In a separate statement issued by CelcomDigi, the telco says it will bring its scale, nationwide network assets and more than 30 years of telecommunications experience to support DNB. This includes leveraging on existing infrastructure, sites and capabilities to drive cost efficiencies, support coverage expansion and accelerate indoor 5G deployment.
